analyst_view.overall: Two struggling sides meet on Monday night: Monza are 18th with 7 points after losing four of five, and Fiorentina (Paolo Vanoli) are 15th with 9 points after three games unbeaten. Ivan Juric is banned from the bench for one game (third sanction) so assistant Matteo Paro leads Monza, and one local report says a fifth straight defeat could cost Juric his job. Monza have Pessina and Ziolkowski back in the squad (Pessina likely on the bench), Robinson fit despite an adductor niggle and Varela up front, but Maye and Folorunsho (counted) are out and Ngonge has joined the injury list with a muscle problem. Fiorentina call 22 with Atta back after two months, Ranieri available, and Njie and Ndour declared recovered; only Pongracic and Parisi (both counted) stay out. Referee Daniele Doveri is one of the most lenient in Serie A (2.7 cards a game), which the numbers already count.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals, already adding a little for both sides' recent scoring and leaky defending and taking about 4% off Fiorentina for Pongracic. Fiorentina are now close to full strength with Njie, Ndour, Atta and Ranieri back, while Monza lose Ngonge, who was not expected to start, and keep their main scorer Varela; nothing moves the total, so about 3.1.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.5 corners, already nudging up for Fiorentina's recent corner count. Monza's wing-back 3-4-2-1 with Birindelli and Mangas and Fiorentina's 4-2-3-1 with Mastantuono and Njie wide are both sides' usual shapes, so I stay at about 8.5.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.3 cards, already cut by about 29% for Doveri's lenient record, which I don't size again. This is a relegation scrap with Juric banned from the touchline and his job reportedly at risk, and a Monza win would lift them level with Fiorentina; games like that tend to bring more fouls than a usual Doveri match, so a mild lean up to about 3.4.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.8 shots, already raised for both sides' recent shooting (+9% Monza, +14% Fiorentina). Fiorentina's returns (Njie, Atta, Ranieri) and Monza's need to attack at home under pressure keep the volume up, but that is what the numbers already see, so about 28.8.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.0 shots on target, already lifted around 10% for each side's recent accuracy. Varela leads Monza's line and Pellegrino Fiorentina's with Njie fit behind him, the picture the numbers already have; Ngonge's injury costs Monza only a bench option, so about 10.
